sha: SET-AT-LAUNCH: branch dig-rollback (0f228ec, from 80b3bbd) rebased onto the fleet sha at launch
notes: GHOST BLOCKS, proven 2026-09-29 on the sandbox (Paper 1.21.11, RCON `execute if block` against the bot's blockAt each time). mineflayer 4.37.1 finishDigging writes AIR into the bot's world model when its own timer fires and never rolls back a dig the server refused (no ack handling, sequence always 0), so every refused dig is a PERMANENT ghost: two ore-tunnel stalls were ghosts, and global dig instrumentation tied the stall cell to the one unconfirmed dig. CAUSES MEASURED with a bare client: (1) mineflayer never sends player_loaded, so Paper drops every dig for ~3 s after each join and respawn (START not acked, block not broken; with player_loaded the same dig breaks in ~30 ms) -- the entombment reflex digs inside that window; (2) out-of-reach digs (7 blocks): no packet ever. ABORT does not resync. collectManually's dig_unconfirmed check assumed a re-send and is blind to both. THE FIX (digsync.mjs): one increasing sequence across block_dig/block_place/use_item; each STOP records the block it overwrites; block_change/multi_block_change record the server's word; the ack settles on it or on the prior block; 5 s backstop; chunk loads drop predictions; player_loaded on every spawn; collectManually waits for settlement (+600 ms after a restore, for Paper's delayed destroy). Design and implementation each reviewed by Claude and Codex independently; both rejected the first (timer) design and recommended this one. 18 tests, 13 anchored mutants killed, 204/204. REAL SERVER, bare client with mineflayer's own bot.dig: control 3 refused digs -> 3 ghosts; candidate: early dig broken (player_loaded), 7-block dig restored at its ack in 45 ms, normal dig broken -- client matches server in all three. WHY THE GATE IS CORRECTNESS: deterministic protocol conformance; the dry run shows the outcome (stuck rows) swings -0.31/bot-h on an unchanged 5-bot pool in 2.5 h, so effect is reported, never gated.

licence.note: The baseline has no digsync module and no `_dig_sync`/`_dig_rollback` row kinds. Every canary bot writes a heartbeat every 10 minutes and on disconnect, so rows are certain within the first read.

require.name: stuck bots in the pool (the population a ghost strands)

draw_exposure.note: Fleet-wide 142 `_reflex_stuck` rows on 48 bots in 5 h (09-29 dry run); min 2 keeps a pool with no stuck bots from being drawn.

exposure.note: Ready = canary heartbeats exist AND >= 100 settled digs on the canary (the ledger saw real work) AND control `_reflex_stuck` >= 1.

own_lines.note: CORRECTNESS. The bookkeeping in front of every dig failed on the fleet (the packet still went out, by design). Deterministic; expected 0.
WIRING. A spawn without player_loaded means the handshake did not run and the 3-s dig blackout is still there.
LIVENESS/COVERAGE: every canary bot seen must write the heartbeat. No evidence class: BLOCKS KEEP.
The baseline cannot write these kinds; a control row means the arms are wrong. BLOCKS KEEP.
POSITIVE CONTROL for the outcome query (78 in the dry run). BLOCKS KEEP.

primary.note: REPORTED, NOT GATED: DiD per bot-hour of _reflex_stuck, _entombed_unrecoverable, _support_cache_outvoted; rollbacks per 1,000 digs (the fleet's ghost rate, measured for the first time); backstop and falseRestore shares; repeatMax (>= 10 = a re-dig loop: TRIPWIRE, named in the read); re-deaths within 30 s (Claude review: player_loaded ends the vanilla spawn grace -- TRIPWIRE). dig_unconfirmed failures WILL rise on the canary (collectManually can now see a refused dig): excluded from any failure-class comparison.

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions.
